title: I-Lang Protocol Specification
description:
I-Lang is an AI-native communication protocol that defines a formal vocabulary of 88 verbs, 29 core modifiers plus a 20-key media profile, 25 entities (17 addressable, 8 role), and 13 Greek aliases for structured communication between humans and AI, between AI agents, and within AI internal reasoning.

It introduces two syntaxes: operation syntax [] for executable instructions and declaration syntax :: for behavioral identity. Version 3.0 defines the communication format, version 4.0 adds execution semantics, and version 5.0 adds a trainable judgment layer built on an 11-dimensional judgment vector space governed by four axioms and a three-layer architecture, grounded in fuzzy mathematics.

I-Lang provides the semantic and judgment layer that sits above tool-integration protocols such as Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-discovery protocols such as Google's Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A). MIT licensed.

Release 5.0-pre.2.1.1 is an erratum on the v5.0 preview line. Section 3 of SPEC-v5.0-PRE.md orders conflicts SURVIVAL > EPISTEMIC, and the reference function f_v5 returns M8 at a STEP-1 survival gate before it reaches the epistemic gate. The section 4 abstain rule required M5 whenever the epistemic gate fires, so a vector that hit both gates had no mode that was both schema-valid and consistent with f_v5. The abstain rule now also accepts M8 on a STEP-1 survival hit. Every other mode under the epistemic gate is still rejected, and M5 stays schema-valid. The reference function, its constants and its weights are unchanged, so no gold label changes. The reference judgment validator ships with the same exception and new self-tests.

The grammar validator now reads quoted values as opaque, so a comma, equals sign or bracket inside a quoted value no longer raises E302 or E304, and its canon gate also lints SPEC-v4.1-MEDIA-PROFILE.md.

Earlier versions: 5.0-pre.2.1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22728994) and 4.1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22729246), both 2026-09-12.
